rubric.text: Establishes structure before instruments - legal form, establishment per country, licences held - and asks only what the profile lacks.
Treats the missing banking licence as the deal-breaker it is and works it per jurisdiction (applicant type is formal; goodwill does not move it).
Germany: explains the Hausbank principle (KfW and the Buergschaftsbanken guarantee through the borrower's house bank), so the route runs through a partner bank, cited.
Italy: names authorised financial-intermediary status under Art. 106 TUB as what opens the Fondo di Garanzia per le PMI, cited.
France: researches and cites the Bpifrance guarantee mechanics (guarantees to banks / credit institutions; Code monetaire et financier), never asserts them from instinct.
EU: InvestEU / EIF guarantees open to alternative lenders as financial intermediaries, cited; flags the move of InvestEU under the European Competitiveness Fund as something to watch.
States where the company stands on each front, and the flags to fix (licence, establishment, sequencing).
Uses precedents - the same fund or institution backing a comparable lender or deal - or says explicitly there is none.
Maps the institutions (regional, national, EU) and names P1/P2 stakeholders per route (head of guarantees / alternative lending), political and public-capital sides.
Prioritises a few routes to run in parallel, with sequencing; parks rather than drops the rest; every recommended or parked route goes on the watchlist.
Saves prioritised next steps and at least one short, formal, strategic outreach draft (the paper-stack test, no AI voice).
Lists instruments before establishing the structure.
Asserts France guarantee mechanics, or any country-specific programme fact, without a citation.
Recommends applying for a banking licence as the default first step without weighing a partnership or intermediary route.
Generalises one country's rule to another.
Walks away from a route without an explicit hard no.
